title: Iman Gadzhi's step-by-step SMMA sales call framework: from setup to closing and collecting cash
summary: Iman breaks down the closing process he taught thousands of agency owners: prepare your environment and research the prospect, choose a one-call or two-call structure, then run Rapport, Pre-frame, Discovery, Transition, Pitch and Close. The core ideas are leading the call with authority, making prospects sell themselves in discovery, and pitching a system rather than a service.

principles.text: Beginners should use a two-call close: discovery first, pitch second. The gap resets prospect energy and lets you tailor the offer.
principles.quote: prospects buy when they are interested and a lot of the time interest is linked directly to energy

principles.text: Pre-frame the call to take authority, show no desperation, and agree upfront on a clear yes or no to avoid "I need to think about it".
principles.quote: at the end of the call I just want a yes or a no let's avoid the maybe

principles.text: In every sales call one person leads with questions and the other follows. As the seller, you must hold the authority to keep the call on track.
principles.quote: in every single sales call there's one person that leads by asking questions and the other that follows by answering them

principles.text: Run discovery on current state, future state, gap, opportunity cost and doubt so the prospect talks themselves into needing you.
principles.quote: remember the key is in the fact that the client says it when you say it it means nothing but when they say it themselves is when your message is hitting

principles.text: Pitch your offer as a system, not a service. Owners see services as expenses and systems as investments, and confused buyers never buy.
principles.quote: business owners can view Services as expenses but they often view systems like Investments

principles.text: State your price with confidence, do not justify it, use silence, then collect cash on the call because a client is only a client once they have paid.
principles.quote: a client is only a client once they have paid
